perf.summary: When k < count, the full HighlyCompositeNumbers list (up to 500 longs) is computed into a stackalloc temp then copied; the copy and the 500-long scratch are unavoidable given the underlying API, but the temp buffer can be sized/justified and the copy skipped when result could be passed directly.
perf.currentCost: 4000 bytes of stackalloc temp plus a copy loop of writeCount longs, even though HighlyCompositeNumbers.Run already writes into a caller buffer.
perf.proposedChange: If k >= the maximum possible count (HCN under limit is bounded, ~a few dozen), write directly into result and skip temp entirely; otherwise call HighlyCompositeNumbers.Run with result as the target and only fall back to temp when k could be smaller than count. Alternatively pass result as the scratch result buffer and truncate in place (no copy) since HCN output is already sorted and result is the consumer.
perf.rationale: Removes a 4 KB stack frame and an O(writeCount) copy in the common path. HCN's count under 2e16 is small and bounded, so result can often be the direct sink, eliminating duplicate storage.
perf.risk: Requires result to have capacity >= count (not just k) if writing HCN output directly; guard with the known upper bound on HCN count under the fixed limit, or keep temp only when result capacity < count. Behavior preserved (same first writeCount sorted values).
